title: CTO Interview Kevin Robinson, VP of Operations, yieldHUB
gist: yieldHUB's VP of Operations Kevin Robinson argues that the AI boom has made semiconductor test floors a supply-chain bottleneck, with tester equipment itself capacity-constrained, so software that mines tester product data to find idle time is the fastest way to add test capacity without new hardware.

insights.claim: Semiconductor test floors worldwide are becoming a supply-chain bottleneck because AI-driven demand for both AI chips and power management chips has filled them to capacity.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Back-end test capacity, not just wafer fabs, is a binding constraint on AI chip output — a signal for test equipment and OSAT pricing power.
insights.quote: With the global AI boom, test floors all over the world are becoming one of the bottlenecks in the supply chain

insights.claim: Test equipment needed to expand semiconductor test capacity is itself subject to the same capacity constraints, with lengthening lead times, so the normal route of buying more testers is effectively closed.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Long tester lead times imply sustained backlog for ATE vendors and a market for capacity-unlocking software.

insights.claim: Semiconductor test floor operators face simultaneously rising demand, equipment costs, equipment delivery times, energy costs and labor costs, meaning each percentage point of operational efficiency gained becomes more valuable every year.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Rising cost pressure supports durable demand and pricing for test-efficiency software.

themes.theme: Gap between MES and tester health tools

insights.claim: yieldHUB identifies a gap in test-floor tooling: MES systems track lot movement and scheduling, and tester-health systems like Advantest's ACS and Teradyne's keep testers running, but neither detects when a loaded, operational tester is actually idle and not testing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines a niche between MES vendors and ATE vendors that a data-analytics player can own.
insights.quote: the tester is loaded, it is operational, it has a product, but it is still actually idle and not testing

insights.claim: MES operators generally know little about product test data, and tester vendors execute customer-written test programs, so neither is positioned to use tester product data to measure test efficiency.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why incumbents have not closed the idle-time gap, supporting a defensible position for independent analytics vendors.

insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Product-agnostic deployment suggests scalability across customers and test floors.

themes.theme: Software vs. hardware and test-program fixes

insights.claim: Changing semiconductor test programs to improve efficiency is slow and expensive because every change requires re-qualification and QA steps; one customer estimated doing it via test programs would take two to three years.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Test-program inertia makes overlay software the faster lever, shortening sales cycles for vendors like yieldHUB.
insights.quote: doing this through the test programs would take two to three years to make the changes and deploy them

insights.claim: On the same customer test floor where a test-program approach was estimated at two to three years, yieldHUB deployed its solution in a couple of weeks within a three-month pilot.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Fast time-to-value is a key adoption driver when capacity is scarce.
insights.quote: we were able to deploy this in a couple of weeks, because we ran a three-month pilot there
